_howToEdit: Each block between { and } is one place. Change the text between the quotes. Keep the commas between blocks. category must be one of: industry, fair, museum, craft, food, transport. locationPrecision is exact or approximate. lastVerified: write the date you checked, e.g. 2026-11-02.

places.name: Rahmi M. Koç Museum
places.description: A large museum of industry, transport and communications on the Golden Horn, with engines, vehicles, machinery and scientific instruments.
places.whyItMatters: A hands-on look at the history of machines and manufacturing in Turkey and beyond. Good for spotting early moulded parts in vintage vehicles, radios and household objects.
places.bestTime: Weekday mornings are usually quieter. [Verify: opening days and hours on the official site]
places.howToGetThere: On the north shore of the Golden Horn in the Hasköy area. Reach it by taxi or by the Golden Horn ferry line. [Verify: current ferry route and stop]

places.name: TÜYAP Fair Convention and Congress Center
places.description: One of Istanbul's main exhibition centres, on the western side of the city, run by the trade fair organiser TÜYAP.
places.whyItMatters: Venue for large industry shows, including the plastics industry fair Plast Eurasia Istanbul. A fair is the easiest way to meet many moulders, material suppliers and press makers in one day.
places.bestTime: During a relevant trade fair. [Verify: fair dates and venue on the organiser's official site]
places.howToGetThere: On the European side, west of the city centre. Reachable by Metrobüs or taxi; allow plenty of time in traffic. [Verify: nearest public transport stop]

places.name: Bursa automotive and supplier cluster
places.description: Bursa is one of Turkey's main automotive cities, with vehicle plants and a wide supplier base in its organised industrial zones. This marker shows the city, not a specific site.
places.whyItMatters: Automotive suppliers use compression moulding for SMC panels, rubber seals and mounts, and other thermoset parts. Factory visits are only possible by prior arrangement with each company.
places.bestTime: Weekdays outside public and religious holidays, when plants are working. Spring and autumn are pleasant for sightseeing.
places.howToGetThere: From Istanbul by road (about 2 to 3 hours depending on traffic) or by fast ferry across the Sea of Marmara plus a bus or taxi connection. [Verify: current ferry operators and timetables]

places.name: Kütahya ceramics town
places.description: Kütahya has a long tradition of hand-painted tiles and pottery (çini) and is also home to modern ceramic tile and sanitaryware production. This marker shows the city centre.
places.whyItMatters: Modern ceramic tiles are formed by pressing powder in a die, a close relative of compression moulding. Here you can compare industrial pressing with traditional hand-formed and hand-painted work.
places.bestTime: Spring to autumn. [Verify: dates of any local ceramics festival]
places.howToGetThere: By road or train via Eskişehir, or by intercity bus from Istanbul, Ankara and Bursa. [Verify: current train services]

places.name: Istanbul Airport (IST)
places.description: Istanbul's main international airport on the European side, and the most likely arrival point for an international visitor.
places.whyItMatters: The starting point for most trips. Domestic flights connect to Izmir, Ankara, Kayseri and other cities on the itinerary.
places.bestTime: Year-round. Leave extra time at public holidays, which are the busiest travel periods.
places.howToGetThere: Metro line M11 runs to the city, and airport buses and taxis are also available. [Verify: current metro and bus routes]
